Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon). NxLabs currently has only 119 real (of 124 seeded) mod catalog entries, hand-picked, across 5 game families (minecraft, rust, valheim, cs2, palworld). The owner wants genuine SCALE — "a massive collection" — not a small curated sample. Build a real bulk-import pipeline against Modrinth's actual public API, which is fully documented and already integrated (a working `MODRINTH_API_KEY` is in `/opt/nxeon/.env`, and `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` already calls this API for per-mod verification — read it first to reuse its request patterns/rate-limit handling rather than reinventing).

## Real scale available (already researched, confirmed live against the real API)
- Modrinth has **157,981 total projects**: ~75,854 mods, ~35,115 resourcepacks, ~18,406 modpacks, ~17,851 plugins, ~14,671 datapacks, ~904 shaders (Minecraft only, all project types).
- Rate limit: **300 requests/minute**, same with or without the API key (the key doesn't raise it, it just avoids being blocked as an unidentified client — send a real identifying `User-Agent`, e.g. `Nxeon/1.0 (mods@nxeon.cloud)` or similar contact-bearing string).
- Bulk endpoint: `GET https://api.modrinth.com/v2/search?facets=[[...]]&limit=100&offset=N` — `limit` caps at 100 server-side even if you ask for more; supports deep pagination (verified working at offset 157000+). Facets include `project_type`, `categories` (loaders live here too), `versions` (game version), and critically **`environment`** (values: `client_and_server`, `server_only`, `dedicated_server_only`, `server_only_client_optional`, `client_or_server`, `client_or_server_prefers_both`, `singleplayer_only`, `client_only`, `client_only_server_optional`, `unknown`) — this is the field that tells you whether something is actually installable on a DEDICATED SERVER, which is what Nxeon hosts. Also `open_source`, `license`, `downloads`, `follows` facets.
- Each search hit already includes: `project_id/slug`, `title`, `description`, `icon_url`, `downloads`, `follows`, `categories`, `license` (an object with `id` as an SPDX identifier or `LicenseRef-*` custom id), `game_versions`, `versions` (list of version ids), `color` (a nice free UI accent).
- `GET /v2/project/{id}` for the full record adds `gallery[]` (real screenshot URLs, hotlinkable, CDN-hosted with `public, max-age=86400` caching and `access-control-allow-origin: *`), `body` (full markdown description), team/author resolution via `GET /v2/team/{id}`.
- `GET /v2/project/{id}/version` gives real per-version `files[]` (direct download URL + sha1/sha512 hash + size), `dependencies[]` (`{project_id, version_id, dependency_type: required|optional|incompatible|embedded}`), `game_versions[]`, `loaders[]`, `version_type` (release/beta/alpha).

## Terms — proceed, but do the one prudent thing first
Modrinth's Terms of Use grant *"a limited, non-exclusive... license to download, display, query... the User Generated Content... via their own services"* for API users — this legitimately covers what NxLabs already does (display + fetch-on-install, never mirroring files). There's a separate, boilerplate "personal non-commercial use only" clause elsewhere in the same document that was clearly written for the website, not the API, and is inconsistent with Modrinth's own public list of commercial third-party integrations (their own `awesome` GitHub list). Before running a full-scale import, send one email to `support@modrinth.com` (draft it, but do NOT send it yourself — hand it back to me in your report so the owner can review/send it) describing: Nxeon is a game-hosting platform, uses the public API to display real mod metadata/images with attribution and to fetch files server-side only when a customer clicks install (never mirroring/rehosting), and asks for written confirmation this is fine at scale. Proceed with building and running the import regardless — this is a courtesy/paper-trail step, not a blocker, since the API is explicitly public and third-party tools are Modrinth's own stated ecosystem.

## What to actually build

1. **A real bulk-import script** (e.g. `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`), separate from the existing per-mod `verify-gamemods.ts` (which stays as the re-verification/freshness-check tool for already-imported mods). This new script should:
   - Query Modrinth's search endpoint across all six real project types (mod, plugin, resourcepack, shader, datapack, modpack — exclude `minecraft_java_server`, that's Modrinth's own server-listing product, not installable content), filtered to `environment` values that are actually server-relevant (`server_only`, `dedicated_server_only`, `server_only_client_optional`, `client_and_server`, `client_or_server`, `client_or_server_prefers_both` — exclude pure `client_only`/`singleplayer_only` content, since Nxeon hosts dedicated servers).
   - Paginate through real results respecting the 300 rpm limit (add real backoff/retry on 429s).
   - For each result, create/upsert a real `GameMod` row (matching the existing schema's `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` convention) with real `iconUrl`, `downloads`, `license`, `galleryUrls` (fetch the full project record for this), `authorName`/`authorAvatarUrl` (resolve via team lookup), `gameVersions`, `loaders`, `verifiedAt`, `upstreamOk: true`, `source: "modrinth"`, `sourceId`.
   - Decide and implement a sensible cutoff so this doesn't try to import literally all 75,854 Minecraft mods in one run and produce a mostly-dead long-tail catalog — a reasonable default is import everything above some real minimum quality bar (e.g. `downloads > 1000` OR `follows > 50`, tune as you see fit) which should still land in the many-thousands range, genuinely "massive" compared to the current 119, while staying real and relevant. Make the threshold a script constant/argument so it can be re-run with a different cutoff later, not hardcoded deep in the logic.
   - Idempotent — safe to re-run, updates existing rows rather than duplicating.
   - Log real progress and a final real count summary (how many imported per project type, how many skipped as duplicates, how many failed).

2. **Expand game-family coverage using other real sources already researched, if time allows** (lower priority than a solid Minecraft import — do Minecraft first and thoroughly, then attempt these if you have room):
   - **Valheim via Thunderstore**: `GET https://thunderstore.io/c/valheim/api/v1/package/` — one unpaginated JSON array (~11,459 real packages last checked), fully unauthenticated, `cache-control: max-age=30`. Each record: `name, full_name, owner, versions[]` where each version has `icon` (gcdn URL), `description`, `download_url`, `downloads`, `dependencies[]` (exact pinned strings), `file_size`. No license field exists on Thunderstore — store `upstreamOk: true` but leave license null/unknown rather than guessing.
   - **Factorio via the official mod portal**: `GET https://mods.factorio.com/api/mods?page_size=100&page=N` (paginated, ~23,317 real mods), and `GET /api/mods/{name}/full` for the complete record including a real `license: {id, name, url}` object and `thumbnail`. No API key needed for metadata. Note: actual file downloads require a user's own Factorio credentials (`?username=&token=`) — for THIS import, only pull metadata/images, don't attempt downloads.
   - Only build these if the Minecraft importer is solid and tested first — do not spread thin across three half-working importers.

3. **Run the real import against production** once tested on staging, and report real final numbers.

## What NOT to do
Do not fabricate any data for imported mods — every field must trace to the real API response. Do not attempt CurseForge (separate legal/technical gate already flagged, not resolved), Nexus Mods (their terms explicitly prohibit this), or Steam Workshop bulk import (needs a Steam Web API key + per-app feasibility testing, out of scope here). Do not modify or regress the existing `GameMod`/`ServerMod`/ratings/comments schema and functionality already shipped — this is additive.

## Process
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Test the import script against a small slice first (e.g. one project type, low limit) before running it at full scale, and verify a handful of resulting `GameMod` rows render correctly on the real NxLabs pages (spot-check via Playwright: does a newly-imported mod show up with a real icon/downloads/license on `/mods`?).
- Check CLAUDE.md's build-isolation rule — don't build directly in /opt/nxeon.
- Credential hygiene: DB reads/writes via `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run via `npx tsx`. Never print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` string — this has leaked the production DB password multiple times this session.
- This is a data-import task, not primarily a deploy task, but if you add/change the schema (e.g. new fields the bulk importer needs that per-mod verify doesn't), follow the normal deploy pipeline for the schema/code change: commit → push → deploy-staging.sh → verify 200 → promote-production.sh → verify 200 and a fresh BUILD_ID. Then run the actual bulk import as a one-off script execution against the production DB (not part of the request/response cycle — a long-running background script is fine, just don't block a deploy on it finishing). A separate agent may be concurrently fixing visual bugs on these same pages — if you see uncommitted changes that aren't yours, don't discard them, only touch your own files (the importer script, schema additions, seed/import tooling).

Report back: the real final count of imported mods (broken down by project type and, if you got to it, by additional game family), the quality-threshold you chose and why, confirmation of idempotency (re-run doesn't duplicate), the drafted (not sent) Modrinth support email text, and confirmation of any schema/code deploy plus the actual import run's real numbers against production.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

REF="${1:-main}"

git fetch origin

npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker

echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
